fact: A World Bank implementation mission visited Uganda's National CERT, among other sites, to assess progress under the UDAP-GovNet project; mission dates are not given, so the published date is used.

NITA-U's executive director said NITA-U built on the foundation laid by the National Information Security Strategy of 2011 (period not stated); the 2014 framework was developed under it and endorsed by Presidential Security Directive No. 1 of 2014.

The NITA-U National Information Security Policy 2026 states that the Uganda National Cybersecurity Strategy (2022-2026), developed by the Government through the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance, is in place and that the policy translates its objectives into mandatory requirements.

The document defines CERT-UG as Uganda's national computer emergency response team, operated under NITA-U, providing incident coordination, vulnerability advisories and threat intelligence, and states it functions as the national CSIRT; the document gives no date of creation, so its publication date is used.

The policy, stated to be mandatory for operators of critical information infrastructure, requires MDAs, local governments and critical infrastructure operators to report information security breaches to the National CSIRT/CERT-UG; this is a national policy requirement, and the document lists no designated CII operators.

The World Bank restructuring paper lists an activity to enhance the National CERT Forensic Laboratory with mobile forensic kits (US$600,000), which presupposes an existing national CERT; no date given for the CERT, so the paper's published date is used.

The Uganda National CERT and Coordination Center (CERT.UG/CC) issued a critical advisory on the SharePoint 'ToolShell' spoofing and remote code execution chain, recommending Microsoft's mitigations and upgrades.
Uganda's National CERT.UG/CC published an advisory on the global CrowdStrike-related IT outage, with recommendations and a call to report incidents to it.
